profile.summary: GenomeOcean is a family of generative DNA language models trained on co-assembled environmental metagenomes, mainly microbial DNA. It reads DNA split into multi-base tokens and predicts the next token. The developers provide scripts to produce sequence embeddings for analysis and to generate new DNA from a prompt. The largest model has 4 billion parameters and reads up to about 50,000 bases.

summary_quotes.text: a 4-billion-parameter generative model trained on 219 TB of diverse, co-assembled global environmental metagenomic data using an optimized transformer
genomeocean: a pretrained microbial genome foundational model (genomeoceanLLM)
It is trained with Causal Language Modeling (CLM) and uses a BPE tokenizer with 4096 tokens. It supports a maximum sequence length of 10240 tokens (~50kbp).

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GenomeOcean is a decoder-only transformer trained by causal language modelling: it predicts the next token from the tokens before it. DNA is split by a BPE tokenizer with 4096 tokens, so 1024 tokens cover about 5,100 bp. The 4B checkpoint uses the Mistral architecture in transformers, with 24 layers, hidden size 3072, 12 attention heads and 4 key/value heads. The package uses vLLM for fast generation and also produces sequence embeddings. The developers report that the model captures universal phylogenetic syntax and protein-coding fidelity, and that its embeddings have low intrinsic dimensionality.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three base models are published: GenomeOcean-100M and GenomeOcean-500M with a 1024-token context, and GenomeOcean-4B with a 10240-token context. Two fine-tuned 4B models exist: GenomeOcean-4B-bgcFM, trained on 11M biosynthetic gene cluster sequences, and GenomeOcean-4B-Artificial-Detector, a classifier for GenomeOcean-generated sequences. The developers recommend the 4B model for general use. The package recently moved to the vLLM V1 engine and transformers 5.12 or later; under transformers 5, the tokenizer should be loaded with PreTrainedTokenizerFast. A result should name the checkpoint, its Hugging Face revision, and the package commit; this page read GenomeOcean-4B at revision 2bed2fc3 and the code at commit 06fa4331.

run_guide.summary: Install the GenomeOcean package with uv at a pinned commit and run the README's embedding example on the bundled sample sequences with GenomeOcean-4B.
prerequisites: Python 3.10 to 3.12 (tested by the developers), git, and uv. The developers recommend their Docker or Apptainer images instead, because of the CUDA and vLLM dependencies.
An NVIDIA GPU with CUDA. The memory needed for GenomeOcean-4B is not stated; the README suggests the 100M or 500M models when GPU memory is limited.
Code and weights are under a BSD-style licence. The weights are not gated.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/jgi-genomeocean/genomeocean.git
cd genomeocean
git checkout --detach 06fa433169539a3c84d7366a663933b888a5386b
steps.explanation: The README does not give a clone command; the clone, cd and checkout lines are added because the later commands run inside the repository. The checkout pins the commit this page was written from.

quotes.text: Please see our official implementation on our [Github](https://github.com/jgi-genomeocean/genomeocean).

steps.title: Install uv
steps.explanation: The README's uv install command for macOS and Linux.

steps.title: Create the environment and install the package
steps.shell:
uv venv GO --python 3.12
source GO/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[all]"
steps.explanation: Creates a Python 3.12 environment and installs GenomeOcean with all dependencies, including vLLM and torch.

steps.title: Embed the sample sequences
steps.shell:
cd examples
python embedding_sequences.py \
    --model_dir pGenomeOcean/GenomeOcean-4B \
    --sequence_file ../sample_data/dna_sequences.txt \
    --model_max_length 10240 \
    --batch_size 10 \
    --output_file outputs/embeddings.npy
steps.explanation: Downloads GenomeOcean-4B and writes one embedding per sequence in the sample file.

outputs: examples/outputs/embeddings.npy, holding the embeddings of the sample sequences.
